The [president of Nauru](/wiki/President_of_Nauru "President of Nauru") is elected by [Parliament](/wiki/Parliament_of_Nauru "Parliament of Nauru") from among its members, and is both the head of state and the head of government of [Nauru](/wiki/Nauru "Nauru"). Nauru's [unicameral](/wiki/Unicameralism "Unicameralism") Parliament has 19 members, with an electoral term of three years. [Political parties](/wiki/List_of_political_parties_in_Nauru "List of political parties in Nauru") only play a minor role in Nauru politics, and there have often been periods of instability in the Presidential office. Shifting allegiances among a small number of individuals can lead to frequent changes in the makeup of the government, including who occupies the office of the president.

Between 1942 and 1945, there were four main [areas of conflict](/wiki/Theater_(military) "Theater (military)") in the Pacific War: China, the [Central Pacific](/wiki/Pacific_Ocean_theater_of_World_War_II "Pacific Ocean theater of World War II"), [South-East Asia](/wiki/South-East_Asian_theatre_of_World_War_II "South-East Asian theatre of World War II") and the [South West Pacific](/wiki/South_West_Pacific_theatre_of_World_War_II "South West Pacific theatre of World War II"). US sources refer to two theaters within the Pacific War: the Pacific theater and the [China Burma India Theater](/wiki/China_Burma_India_Theater_of_World_War_II "China Burma India Theater of World War II") (CBI). However, these were not operational commands.

In the Pacific, the Allies divided operational control of their forces between two supreme commands, known as [Pacific Ocean Areas](/wiki/Pacific_Ocean_Areas_(command) "Pacific Ocean Areas (command)") and [Southwest Pacific Area](/wiki/South_West_Pacific_Area_(command) "South West Pacific Area (command)").[[55]](#cite_note-63)

The [Imperial Japanese Navy](/wiki/Imperial_Japanese_Navy_in_World_War_II "Imperial Japanese Navy in World War II") (IJN) did not integrate its units into permanent theater commands. The [Imperial Japanese Army](/wiki/Imperial_Japanese_Army "Imperial Japanese Army") (IJA), which had already created the [Kwantung Army](/wiki/Kwantung_Army "Kwantung Army") to oversee its occupation of Manchukuo and the [China Expeditionary Army](/wiki/China_Expeditionary_Army "China Expeditionary Army") during the Second Sino-Japanese War, created the [Southern Expeditionary Army Group](/wiki/Southern_Expeditionary_Army_Group "Southern Expeditionary Army Group") at the outset of its conquests of South East Asia. This headquarters controlled the bulk of the Japanese Army formations which opposed the Western Allies in the Pacific and South East Asia.

The flora of the Sahara is highly diversified based on the bio-geographical characteristics of this vast desert. [Floristically](/wiki/Floristics "Floristics"), the Sahara has three zones based on the amount of rainfall received – the Northern (Mediterranean), Central and Southern Zones. There are two transitional zones – the Mediterranean-Sahara transition and the Sahel transition zone.[[50]](#cite_note-Mares1999-50)

The Saharan flora comprises around 2800 species of [vascular plants](/wiki/Vascular_plant "Vascular plant"). Approximately a quarter of these are [endemic](/wiki/Endemism "Endemism"). About half of these species are common to the flora of the Arabian deserts.[[51]](#cite_note-Houérou2008-51)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7c/GueltaCamels.jpg/250px-GueltaCamels.jpg)](/wiki/File:GueltaCamels.jpg)

Camels in the [Guelta d'Archei](/wiki/Guelta_d%27Archei "Guelta d'Archei"), in north-eastern [Chad](/wiki/Chad "Chad")

The central Sahara is estimated to include five hundred species of plants, which is extremely low considering the huge extent of the area. Plants such as acacia trees, palms, succulents, spiny shrubs, and grasses have adapted to the arid conditions, by growing lower to avoid water loss by strong winds, by storing water in their thick stems to use it in dry periods, by having long roots that travel horizontally to reach the maximum area of water and to find any surface moisture, and by having small thick leaves or needles to prevent water loss by [evapotranspiration](/wiki/Evapotranspiration "Evapotranspiration"). Plant leaves may dry out totally and then recover.

Several species of fox live in the Sahara including: the [fennec fox](/wiki/Fennec_fox "Fennec fox"), [pale fox](/wiki/Pale_fox "Pale fox") and [Rüppell's fox](/wiki/R%C3%BCppell%27s_fox "Rüppell's fox"). The [addax](/wiki/Addax "Addax"), a large white [antelope](/wiki/Antelope "Antelope"), can go nearly a year in the desert without drinking.
